q: My horizon is a bit crooked in the beach shot. How do I straighten it?
a: 1. Select the clip and open Effect Controls: Motion is built in, no effect to apply. 2. Set Rotation (`effects.setParam`, effect `motion`, param `rotation`) a degree or two against the tilt: if the horizon drops to the right, a small positive or negative value levels it; check it against a straight line near the horizon. 3. Rotating uncovers black corners: raise Scale (param `scale`) until they are filled and watch the frame edges (for 2° on a 16:9 frame about 107 % is enough). 4. The scale-up crops a little and softens the picture slightly, so use the smallest rotation and scale that do the job.

q: how do i fix a tilted video, the sea is going downhill lol
a: Straighten it with Motion in Effect Controls (it's on every clip already): turn Rotation a degree or two the opposite way to the tilt (`effects.setParam`, param `rotation`) until the sea is level, then raise Scale (param `scale`) until the black corners rotation shows are gone. Go only as far as needed: every bit of scale-up crops the edges.

q: Handheld walk where the horizon slowly drifts from level to about 3 degrees off. Can I level it over the shot rather than with one setting?
a: Yes, animate Motion's Rotation: 1. At the start, click the Rotation stopwatch (`effects.toggleAnimation`, effect `motion`, param `rotation`) with the value that levels it there. 2. Move the playhead to where the tilt peaks and set the value that levels it (`effects.setParam`: with animation on, a change at another time adds a keyframe); add more keyframes where the drift changes direction. 3. Set Scale (param `scale`) high enough to hide the corners at the largest rotation (about 3° needs roughly 110 % on 16:9), one value for the whole shot so the framing doesn't breathe. 4. Ease the keyframes (`effects.setInterpolation`, Auto Bezier) so the correction doesn't jerk. If the walk also shakes, Warp Stabilizer (`effects.apply`) steadies it first; level after.

q: Resolve user here: where's the equivalent of Inspector Rotation Angle plus Zoom for levelling a horizon?
a: In Revolution it's Motion in Effect Controls, on every clip without applying anything: Rotation (degrees) is Resolve's Rotation Angle and Scale is its Zoom. Rotate a degree or two against the tilt (`effects.setParam`, effect `motion`, param `rotation`), then raise Scale (param `scale`) until the corners are filled. Both can be keyframed with the stopwatch (`effects.toggleAnimation`) if the tilt changes during the shot.

q: How do I end my video with an old TV switch-off effect, where the picture squashes into a line and disappears?
a: 1. On the last clip, open Effect Controls ▸ Motion and turn Uniform Scale off (`effects.setParam`, effect `motion`, param `uniform_scale`, `false`): Scale now sets the height and Scale Width the width. 2. A few frames before the end, click the Scale stopwatch (`effects.toggleAnimation`, param `scale`) at 100. 3. Move about 5 frames later and set Scale to 1 (`effects.setParam`): the picture squeezes to a thin full-width line (at 1 % about 11 px tall on 1080p) over black. 4. For the dot at the end, keyframe Scale Width (param `scale_width`) from 100 down to almost 0 over the next few frames, then let the clip end on black. 5. Ease In on the keyframes (`effects.setInterpolation`) makes the squeeze snap the way an old set does; a short click or hum cut on an SFX track sells it.

q: In Premiere I'd untick Uniform Scale and keyframe Scale Height for a CRT power-off. Same in Revolution?
a: Nearly: Motion has Uniform Scale too (`effects.setParam`, param `uniform_scale`, `false`), but there's no separate Scale Height: with Uniform Scale off, Scale is the height and Scale Width is the width. So keyframe Scale (`effects.toggleAnimation` then `effects.setParam`, param `scale`) from 100 to about 1 over 4–6 frames for the line, then Scale Width (param `scale_width`) toward 0 for the dot. For the whole CRT look before it switches off, the VHS shader (Video Effects ▸ User ▸ Stylize) adds scanlines; it runs only on the GPU.
